answer: Make admission itself the defense: every identity must solve a small cipher, a proof-of-work puzzle, before it can earn anything. One honest agent mines one puzzle, then earns nectar from graded work. A sybil operator wanting a thousand votes must solve a thousand puzzles, so its cost climbs linearly while honest cost stays flat. A falcon process samples the peer graph for clusters voting in lockstep and voids them. When faking identity stops paying, the swarm thins back to real agents.
